notes: EXPERIMENTAL TESTER ENTRY: nothing of this record was measured by Contour's maintainer. It exists so that one owner of a TP65 can try Contour on their unit and report what it does (https://github.com/Chronosauros/contour/issues/6). It is not a supported device. The read-only 1.8.0-tp65test2 passed on the unit (issue comment, 26.11.2026: firmware 0.4, all ten bands and the preamp equal to the Windows reads byte for byte, the same after a replug, Android HID interface 0, IN 0x86, OUT 0x05). Since 1.8.1-tp65test3 a release or beta build writes it with the TP65's own sequence (WalkPlayProfiles.TP65_TESTER_WRITE true, WalkPlay.tp65WriteSequence); 1.8.0-tp65test1 offered HOLD TO SEND through the Space II's sequence

unit evidence from its owner (Windows, firmware 0.4; issue #6 attachment EPZ-TP65-Contour-Contribution.zip, 25.11.2026): VID 0x3302, PID 0x4325, manufacturer string "EPZ Technology", product string "TP65", bcdDevice 0x0001, HID interface MI_00, usage page 0x0C, 64-byte input and output reports with report ID 0x4B; reads answered: version 80 0C 00 ("0.4"), the slot byte 80 09 00 (0, twice), ten bands 80 09 00 00 i 00 (all PEAK, 0 dB, register Q 0x00B6, 31 / 62 / 125 / 250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000 / 4000 / 8000 / 16000 Hz, coefficients those of a 96 kHz RBJ peak at Q 0.75), the offset / preamp 80 03 01 (reply 80 03 02 00 00, 0), and reads of filter 0x11, work mode 0x1D, output 0x19 and balance 0x16 (none written); one PEAK band written (01 09 18, -1 dB at 1000 Hz) with the RAM apply 01 0A 04 00 00 FF FF read back right and still read after a USB replug with no flash command; two read timeouts on Windows (1200 ms) with no known cause. Never tried on a TP65: the preamp write, 01 05, 01 17, the flash 01 01 01, other filter types, the Android USB transport

catalogs: devicePEQ's usbDeviceConfig.js lists PID 0x4325 in its "SchemeNo16" group (line 702, https://github.com/jeromeof/devicePEQ/blob/0617f382e76629792a5933e6933e4b396a756a93/devicePEQ/usbDeviceConfig.js#L702; peq10Band10dBFullShelves: ten bands, +-10 dB, PEAK and both shelves, Q 0.1-10, deviceHandlesPregain false); FreeDSP-Studio's tools/app/src/dsp2.rs (MIT) lists 0x4325 in `Scheme { no: 16, bands: 10, gain: 10.0, types: SHELVES }` (line 145); no source names the TP65 itself
found by VID, PID and the exact USB product name "TP65" (findDevice); the same PID with any other name matches nothing (another product may use PID 0x4325)

the record is the catalog's range on the Tanchjim Space II's read code and conventions (a measured unit of the same scheme): ten bands, +-10 dB, Q 0.1-10, 96 kHz coefficient design, preamp -30..0 dB in whole dB, the Space II's lenient preamp reply header. PEAK only: the catalog's LOW_SHELF and HIGH_SHELF are held (peq.heldTypes), no shelf was written on a TP65. The preamp is read with 80 03 01 (DeviceProtocol.preampRequest), the form read on the unit, not the 80 03 00 of the other WalkPlay DACs, and never written: a send needs the profile's preamp to equal what the DAC holds (0 dB on the unit) and is refused before the first frame otherwise. LOW_PASS, HIGH_PASS and +-12 dB (taken by the Space II and the Max) stay candidates for a measured unit

no DAC settings: the record has no settings rows, so the DAC Settings page is empty and Contour sends no gain, filter, work mode, balance or mic frame and never report 0x54 to this unit. WalkPlayGuard holds the TP65 to an allow-list in every context: the reads 80 0C 00, 80 09 00, 80 09 00 00 i 00 and 80 03 01, the band write 01 09 18 00 i 00 00 and the RAM apply 01 0A 04 00 00 FF FF; everything else (the preamp write, 01 05, 01 17, the flash 01 01 x, 01 04, settings, factory reset, firmware, probes) is refused

sequence: connect (every build): version 80 0C 00, the slot byte 80 09 00, ten bands 80 09 00 00 i 00, the preamp 80 03 01; any reply that does not parse stops the read

a send (since 1.8.1-tp65test3): the same full read first, then only the bands whose registers differ from it, each 01 09 18 00 i 00 00 + 20 coefficient bytes + freq, Q, gain, type, 00, slot, 20 ms after it (120 ms after the last); then the RAM apply 01 0A 04 00 00 FF FF and 250 ms; then the same full strict read-back, compared register by register with the plan

never in a send: the preamp write 01 03, 01 05, 01 17, the flash 01 01 01. Its owner saw an edited band still read after a replug with no flash command (Windows), as the Space II keeps band frames without one (A/B session, 16.11.2026); a send whose preamp differs from the DAC's is refused before the first write frame, and a band that reads back different ends the send NOT VERIFIED, never sent again by itself

reset.src: nothing read from a TP65 by Contour; command 0x05 resets are never sent to it

hwVolume.src: the owner reports physical volume control not validated yet; nothing recorded about a UAC Feature Unit or vendor volume control

evidenceCaveats: Two catalog entries (devicePEQ and FreeDSP-Studio, SchemeNo16 by PID), its owner's Windows evidence (issue #6 attachment: reads, one PEAK band write with the RAM apply and its persistence over a replug) and Contour's read of the unit (1.8.0-tp65test2, 26.11.2026). Nothing was written with Contour before 1.8.1-tp65test3. The ranges beyond the read factory flat and the preamp policy are the Space II's and the catalog's, not the TP65's own.

The TP65 write sends only the frames its owner validated (band writes and the RAM apply 01 0A) on the Space II's pacing. Several band frames in one send, gains other than -1 dB, shelves and the DSP output after a Contour write were never tried on a TP65, and persistence rests on one replug on Windows: no flash command is sent.
